title: Analysis of Pelvic Organ Prolapse-related Content on Pinterest
screen_reason: Cross-sectional content analysis of the first 100 relevant Pinterest pins for 'pelvic organ prolapse'. Each pin was compared with IUGA/ICS professional guidelines and rated on an explicit 1-5 misinformation scale; the paper reports a share of items carrying misinformation with a stated denominator ('Misinformation was seen in 27 of 100 pins (score >1)'). That is a CONTENT prevalence estimate against an external ground truth (published clinical guidelines), so the paper is eligible. The paper's primary outcomes (DISCERN quality, PEMAT understandability/actionability) are QUALITY measures and are recorded as such.

estimates.country: not stated (Pinterest search run by US-based investigators, University of Maryland)
estimates.date: not stated; article published online ahead of print 15 September 2020
estimates.measure_type: % of Pinterest pins on pelvic organ prolapse containing any misinformation (misinformation score >1 on a 1-5 scale, judged against IUGA/ICS guidelines)
estimates.value_raw: 27 of 100 pins (score >1); Table 1 misinformation score: (1) None 73, (2) Low to moderate 24, (3) Moderate 3, (4) 0, (5) 0

estimates.definition: A pin scored above 1 on a 1-5 misinformation scale (i.e. any of low-to-moderate, moderate, moderate-to-high, high misinformation) when its content departed from the IUGA/ICS joint report guidelines for discussing and managing pelvic organ prolapse
estimates.misinfo_def: "The presence of misinformation was evaluated using a 1 to 5 scale, ranging from no misinformation to high levels of misinformation to be consistent with the DISCERN criteria scale." (content benchmarked against IUGA/ICS joint report guidelines)
estimates.source_quote: information was seen in 27 of 100 pins (score >1) and commercial
estimates.page_loc: Results, p. e373 (final Results paragraph, right column); Table 1 (Secondary Outcomes, Misinformation Score, n = 100)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two reviewers independently examined each pin and its linked content; misinformation was rated 1-5 against the IUGA/ICS joint report guidelines for POP. No inter-rater reliability statistic is reported, and the authors flag residual subjectivity ('Nonbinary metrics such as quality and metrics evaluated on a continuous scale, such as misinformation, are inherently subject to some reviewer bias').
estimates.moderator_quote: Content was compared with the International Urogynecological Association (IUGA)/International Continence Society (ICS) joint report guidelines for discussing and managing POP.17 The presence of misinformation was evaluated using a 1 to 5 scale, ranging from no misinformation to high levels of misinformation to be consistent with the DISCERN criteria scale.
estimates.notes: Single-topic keyword search truncated at the top 100 relevant results, hence denom_scope=topical with denom_selection=curated. The 27/100 figure is stated verbatim twice in the text ('27 contained some amount of misinformation'), so it is not a sum I computed from Table 1 rows. Data-collection date is nowhere stated; the online-ahead-of-print date (September 2020) is used for year. Country is not stated; Pinterest results are not geographically bounded in the methods, so coded Global. missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted, with reasons: (a) PEMAT understandability <75% in 16/100 pins and PEMAT actionability <75% in 30/100 pins - readability/actionability instruments, not falsity, and not even 'quality' in the information-accuracy sense; one QUALITY row (DISCERN 16) already represents this family. (b) Commercial bias present in 36/100 pins - commercial bias is not misinformation. (c) All subset shares inside the PFMT (n=79) and surgery (n=43) subsamples (e.g. 'Presence of commercial bias 38 (48.1%)', 'Low-to-moderate quality 50 (63.3%)') - these are topic-completeness/quality subsets, and no misinformation share is reported for any subset. (d) 'Compared with IUGA/ICS guidelines, no pins contained more than moderate levels of misinformation' - a zero share for high misinformation; it is the complement of the extracted row's grading and adds no distinct estimate, though it does bound severity. (e) '40% of top links related to common diseases report misinformation' (Discussion) - a figure the paper cites from reference 19, not its own data, so excluded per R8. (f) '>5 million followers' reached by the 100 pins is a reach denominator the authors themselves say they could not use ('we could not definitively quantify the reach of evaluated pins'), so no REACH row.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis of the first 100 relevant pins returned by a single Pinterest search for 'pelvic organ prolapse' (>300 results returned; 34 pins excluded for duplicate linked content n=24, no linked content n=2, purchase-required content n=1, off-topic n=7; sponsored/promoted pins excluded a priori). Two reviewers independently examined each pin and its linked content using DISCERN and 17 of 26 PEMAT items, with misinformation rated 1-5 against IUGA/ICS guidelines; descriptive statistics in STATA SE 15.0. No inter-rater reliability coefficient, no reconciliation procedure and no search date are reported; the authors note results are a single moment in time and that repeat searches gave slightly different top-100 sets.
